messages:
jordan: Quick sync — ran a focused benchmark after the attn-optim + kernel-selector change landed. Wanted to surface anomalies before we ship the rollout.
maya: thanks — short summary?
jordan: p50 looks fine, p95 slightly improved (~6%), but p99 jumped for long sequences (seq=2048) under bursty arrivals. numbers below.
liam: can you paste the commands and raw outputs so I can reproduce?
jordan: sure

```bash
./bench_runner \
  --model gptx-7b \
  --sequence 2048 \
  --batch 1,4,8 \
  --kernels fused_attn,matmul_fallback \
  --iters 500 \
  --measure p50,p95,p99,throughput
```

jordan: summary table (batch=1): p50 24ms -> 22ms, p95 68ms -> 64ms, p99 210ms -> 340ms (regression)
priya: whoa p99 that big. under what load pattern?
jordan: tail spike only seen when we mix cache hits/misses (prefix heavy). If KV cache hit rate < ~60% we see the regression.
maya: hypothesis: fused_attn kernel has a bad fallthrough path for partial KV cache invalidation.
liam: I noticed a similar spike locally when kernel picked tiled-fused for large seqs; fallback to matmul removes the spike but increases avg.
priya: can we add a quick guard: if seq > 1024 and cache_hit_rate < 0.7, force matmul_fallback? low risk short-term.
jordan: implemented a config flag and re-ran: with forced fallback p99 drops back to 215ms; p50+p95 regress ~8% but acceptable for now.
maya: we should add unit test and an integration smoke to catch this pattern. Also want telemetry to annotate kernel decision + cache_hit_rate for any >p95 traces.
liam: agree. I'm worried about quantization interactions — the quantized kernels may amplify numeric noise when we switch kernels mid-request.
priya: did you check correctness diffs (logprobs / top tokens)?
jordan: quick check: token-level disagreement ~0.2% with quantized path on one eval set; within tolerance but we need regression alerting.
maya: action items:
- liam: add trace fields (kernel_choice, cache_hit_rate, seq_len, batch_size) to latency spans (small change) — due EOD.
- priya: add a bench scenario that sweeps cache_hit_rate (1.0 -> 0.0) for seq = [512,1024,2048], batch=1,4 — due tomorrow morning.
- jordan: roll back rollout flag to opt-in and push the temp guard in routing layer (feature flagged) — done in branch, will PR.
- maya: draft an eval to compare top-1 token diffs across kernels + quant configs, hook into quality-monitoring pipeline.

ci-bot: nightly-bench#1719 completed: 171 tests, 3 regressions (p99 tail), see /ci/artifacts/bench/1719 for logs
priya: linking logs: https://internal/bench/1719/results.json
liam: I ran the trace for one of the bad samples — attached stack snippet shows long wait inside fused_attn->reduce_step when key_padding varies per head.
jordan: snippet:

```
[trace] kernel=fused_attn selected
[trace] seq=2048 batch=1 cache_hits=0.42
[trace] enter fused_attn reduce_step 0.0s
[trace] stall 0.12s waiting on matmul-shard-3
[trace] fallback partial matmul executed
```

maya: seems like a cross-shard synchronization issue. Could be scheduling + cuda stream ordering when we mix tiled matmuls and fused kernels.
priya: linked a repro harness: ./bench_runner --mix-requests pattern_file=tests/mix_cache_patterns.json
jordan: next steps I suggest:
- short-term: keep opt-in fused-attn in canary, enable guard (cache_hit_rate + seq_len) to avoid p99 regressions
- mid-term: add a synchronization audit in fused_attn to ensure no hidden dependencies on stream ordering
- long-term: refine kernel cost model to account for cache fragmentation and per-head padding, not just seq_len
maya: 👍 also let's add a regression test that fails CI if p99 increases >15% vs baseline on the sweep.
liam: I'll own the perf baseline update and add the CI gate. small note: set the baseline to median of last 5 runs to reduce noise.
priya: also add an alert that fires when token-level disagreement >0.5% for production traffic after a kernel switch.
jordan: will write the RFC follow-up with concrete telemetry and the rollback criteria. posting PR links when ready.
maya: thanks team. keep thread focused — ping me if you need escalation for infra changes :eyes:
priya: weekly sync note: we'll review progress in tomorrow's runtime standup.
liam: I'll open tickets for the audit + bench scenarios.
jordan: linking my branch: https://repo/infra/attn-kernel-guard/compare
maya: great, closing the loop here. :thumbsup:
